title: Fluency Reset Practice Room
description: Guided speaking workouts that move from supported production to flexible communication.
designPrinciples: Every drill has a communicative purpose, not only a language form.
Every drill moves through setup, first attempt, one focused retry, and reflection.
Support is reduced gradually through Follow, Recall, and Free stages.
Fluency rounds reuse familiar language rather than adding several new items at once.
Repair and interaction strategies are trained directly, including planning, clarification, turn-taking, compensating, and self-correction.
Completion means the message was understandable and achieved its purpose; it does not mean perfect grammar.

tightBuild.label: Tight Build
tightBuild.purpose: Start from one safe sentence and make controlled changes before giving a short message.

items.title: Build a natural introduction

transformations.model: I work in customer support, and I’m currently focusing on problem management.
Before this, I worked in technical consulting.
Outside of work, I’m building a small online business.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Give a 45-second introduction using the three parts.

items.title: Describe the present moment

transformations.model: I’m checking my messages at my desk.
I’m checking my messages because I’m waiting for an update.
After that, I’m going to finish my report.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Narrate what you are doing now and what you will do next.

items.title: Organise today’s plan
items.baseSentence: I need to finish one task.

transformations.model: I need to finish the customer report.
I need to finish the customer report before lunch.
I need to finish it before lunch, but I’m still waiting for the latest figures.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Explain your plan for today in a clear order.

items.title: Describe a routine

transformations.model: I start work at nine, and I usually check urgent tickets first.
I normally have two or three meetings in the morning.
Most days are predictable, but Mondays are usually busier.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Describe a normal workday from start to finish.

items.title: Move a story into the past

transformations.model: Yesterday, I visited a customer.
Yesterday, I visited a customer to understand a system problem.
We found the cause and agreed on the next step.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Tell a short story about something that happened yesterday.

items.title: Expand a weekend answer

transformations.model: My weekend was relaxing.
I spent Saturday with my family.
It was nice because we had not gone out together for a while.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Answer “How was your weekend?” with two useful details.

items.title: Turn confusion into a clear question

transformations.model: I’m not clear about the deadline.
Do you mean we need to finish testing by Thursday?
Once you confirm that, I can update the plan.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Clarify one realistic instruction without sounding defensive.

items.title: Confirm understanding
items.baseSentence: So, I need to update the file.

transformations.model: So, I need to update the file by three o’clock.
Then I should send it to the project team.
Is that correct, or have I missed anything?

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Summarise an instruction and ask for confirmation.

items.title: Agree and contribute

transformations.model: That makes sense because it reduces the risk.
We could also test it with one customer first.
Would that work for everyone?

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Respond to an idea by agreeing and adding one useful point.

items.title: Disagree constructively

transformations.model: I understand why that option looks faster.
However, I’m concerned that we have not tested it enough.
Perhaps we could run a small test before the full release.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Disagree with a proposal while protecting the relationship.

items.title: Structure a first-job story
items.baseSentence: My first job was in retail.

transformations.model: My first job was in a small retail shop after college.
At first, I found it difficult to speak to unhappy customers.
It taught me to listen carefully and explain things calmly.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Tell your first-job story with a beginning, challenge, and lesson.

items.title: Describe an achievement

transformations.model: I completed a difficult system migration.
My team spent several weeks testing and correcting issues.
I’m proud of it because the customer could continue working without disruption.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Describe an achievement and explain why it matters to you.

items.title: Explain a solved problem

transformations.model: Several users could not access the system.
I compared the logs and reproduced the problem in a test environment.
We identified a configuration error and restored access.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Explain a problem, your action, and the result.

items.title: Turn a mistake into a lesson

transformations.model: I sent an update before checking one important detail.
The team had to correct the information later.
Since then, I use a short checklist before sending critical updates.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Share one mistake without making the story sound overly negative.

items.title: Describe an influential person

transformations.model: My manager influenced me because she stayed calm under pressure.
She asked clear questions instead of blaming people.
I now try to use the same approach when supporting my team.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Describe someone who influenced the way you work or think.

items.title: Build follow-up questions

transformations.model: What got you interested in travelling?
What is the most memorable place you have visited?
Do you prefer travelling alone or with other people?

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Keep a conversation going with two connected follow-up questions.

items.title: Close a conversation warmly

transformations.model: It was really nice talking with you.
I need to get back to my desk before the next meeting.
Let’s continue this conversation another time.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: End a friendly conversation without sounding abrupt.

items.title: Build a concise project update

transformations.model: We completed the main configuration yesterday.
At the moment, we are testing the data migration.
The only risk is a delayed file, so I’ll follow up with the customer today.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Give a 60-second update covering progress, risk, and next action.

items.title: Ask for help precisely

transformations.model: Could you help me understand this error message?
I checked the configuration and restarted the service, but the error remains.
Could you review the logs with me for ten minutes?

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Ask for help in a way that makes it easy for someone to respond.

items.title: Confirm a requirement

transformations.model: From my understanding, you need a weekly report.
Is it for managers, and should it be in Excel?
Would you like the first version by Friday?

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Confirm a requirement before beginning the work.

items.title: Recommend with reasons

transformations.model: I recommend this café because it is quiet and easy to reach.
It would suit you if you need somewhere to work.
The food is a little expensive, though.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Recommend a product or place with a benefit and one honest limitation.

items.title: Explain a process clearly

transformations.model: Then choose the account section.
Make sure your email address is correct before continuing.
Once you save it, the system will send a confirmation message.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Explain a simple process using clear sequence markers.

items.title: Give an opinion
items.baseSentence: I think remote work is useful.

transformations.model: I think remote work is useful because it saves travelling time.
For example, I can use that time for focused work.
However, face-to-face meetings are still helpful for complex discussions.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Give a balanced opinion in 60 seconds.

items.title: Compare options fairly

transformations.model: Option A is cheaper, while Option B is easier to maintain.
The trade-off is lower cost versus lower support effort.
For a small team, I would choose Option B.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Compare two options using at least two criteria.

items.title: Recommend a solution

transformations.model: The current handover process causes missing information.
I suggest using a short shared checklist.
That would reduce rework, and we could test it with one team next week.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Recommend a realistic solution and explain how to start.

items.title: Explain a change or trend

transformations.model: Sales increased slightly over the last three months.
This may be because more customers found us through social media.
We should track another month before drawing a firm conclusion.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Describe a simple trend without overstating what the data proves.

items.title: Correct yourself smoothly

transformations.model: Sorry, let me correct that.
The meeting is on Friday at two.
I’ll send the agenda tomorrow morning.

items.finalSpeakingPrompt: Practise correcting one detail and continuing without restarting.

items.followUpQuestion: What made you interested in your current work or hobby?
items.retryFocus: Remove one unnecessary detail and add one clear hook for the listener.
items.braveExtension: Introduce yourself at a networking event, explain a goal, and invite the other person to speak.

items.title: Narrate what you are doing now
items.listenerRole: You are doing an ordinary activity and describe it directly in English.
items.prompt: Narrate the action, reason, and next step.
items.communicativeOutcome: Connect visible actions and intentions to English without translating a prepared paragraph.
keyPoints: What you can see or hear
supportPhrases: The next thing I need to do is…
items.followUpQuestion: What could make this activity easier?
items.retryFocus: Connect ideas with because, so, or but instead of listing sentences.
items.braveExtension: Continue an English inner monologue from actions to plans and feelings.

items.title: Explain today’s plan
items.listenerRole: A colleague or family member asks what you are doing today.
items.prompt: Explain the sequence and one possible difficulty.
items.communicativeOutcome: Explain a realistic plan in an order the listener can follow.
items.followUpQuestion: What will you do if the main task takes longer?
items.retryFocus: Make the order clearer and replace one vague word with a specific noun.
items.braveExtension: Defend your priorities and give a backup plan.

items.title: Describe a normal workday
items.listenerRole: Someone outside your team asks what a typical day is like.
items.prompt: Describe the routine from start to finish and one challenge.
items.communicativeOutcome: Describe a routine clearly without listing every small task.
supportPhrases: Most of my time goes into…
items.followUpQuestion: Which part of your day requires the most communication?
items.retryFocus: Replace one list of duties with a concrete example.
items.braveExtension: Explain it to someone outside your field without jargon.

items.title: Answer “How was your weekend?”
items.listenerRole: A colleague casually asks how your weekend was.
items.prompt: Share one moment, why it mattered, and invite a response.
items.communicativeOutcome: Give more than a one-word answer without turning it into a speech.
items.followUpQuestion: What did you enjoy most?
items.retryFocus: Add one concrete detail that is easy to respond to.
items.braveExtension: Turn the opener into a short story and ask a specific follow-up.

items.title: Buy thinking time naturally
items.listenerRole: Someone asks a question and you need a few seconds to organise your answer.
items.prompt: Answer an opinion question with a reason.
items.communicativeOutcome: Hold the turn politely instead of freezing.
supportPhrases: Let me think for a second.
items.followUpQuestion: Has your answer changed over time?
items.retryFocus: Replace one long hesitation with a deliberate phrase.
items.braveExtension: Answer an unexpected question with two organised points.

items.title: Clarify an unclear instruction
items.listenerRole: An instruction can be understood in two ways.
items.prompt: Restate the instruction, identify the unclear detail, and confirm the action.
items.communicativeOutcome: Identify the ambiguity and obtain a clear next action.
supportPhrases: When you say ___, do you mean…?
items.followUpQuestion: What could happen if you misunderstood?
items.retryFocus: Turn one broad question into a precise either-or question.
items.braveExtension: Clarify scope, timing, and ownership with no more than three questions.

items.title: Agree and add something useful
items.listenerRole: Someone shares an idea you agree with.
items.prompt: Agree, connect an example, and add one next thought.
items.communicativeOutcome: Show genuine agreement and move the conversation forward.
supportPhrases: Another thing we could consider is…
items.followUpQuestion: What would make the idea work well?
items.retryFocus: Replace a general yes with an explanation.
items.braveExtension: Agree with the main point but identify a condition for success.

items.title: Tell the story of your first job
items.listenerRole: Someone asks about your first job or first responsibility.
items.prompt: Tell how you started, one challenge, and the lesson.
items.communicativeOutcome: Tell a compact story with context, challenge, and lesson.
items.followUpQuestion: How does it influence you today?
items.retryFocus: Add one specific action rather than a general description.
items.braveExtension: Tell it as an interview story showing one quality.

items.title: Describe an achievement you are proud of
items.listenerRole: Someone asks about something you achieved.
items.prompt: Explain the goal, action, and visible result.
items.communicativeOutcome: Explain the goal, your contribution, and why it matters.
supportPhrases: One achievement I’m proud of is…
items.followUpQuestion: What was the hardest part?
items.retryFocus: Add one concrete result or before-and-after difference.
items.braveExtension: Give a STAR-style story and connect it to a future goal.

items.title: Share a mistake and what you learned
items.listenerRole: You are asked about a mistake or lesson.
items.prompt: Explain the mistake, repair, and new behaviour.
items.communicativeOutcome: Take responsibility and show how behaviour changed.
items.followUpQuestion: What early sign would help next time?
items.retryFocus: Remove one excuse and add a prevention step.
items.braveExtension: Give an interview-quality answer with prevention.

items.title: Tell a memorable trip or event
items.listenerRole: A friend asks about a trip or event you remember clearly.
items.prompt: Tell one event and your reaction.
items.communicativeOutcome: Create a vivid but concise story with one memorable moment.
supportPhrases: One trip I still remember is…
items.followUpQuestion: Would you recommend it?
items.retryFocus: Add one sensory or emotional detail.
items.braveExtension: Tell it with expectation, surprise, and reflection.

items.title: Describe a person who influenced you
items.listenerRole: Someone asks who influenced how you think or work.
items.prompt: Give an example and explain the impact.
items.communicativeOutcome: Describe the person through one concrete example.
items.followUpQuestion: What would you thank the person for?
items.retryFocus: Replace one general compliment with an action.
items.braveExtension: Tell a story and connect the lesson to today.

items.title: Start small talk from the shared situation
items.listenerRole: You are waiting with someone at work, an event, or a public place.
items.prompt: Open, react to the answer, and ask a follow-up.
items.communicativeOutcome: Open a friendly conversation using something you both observe.
supportPhrases: It’s pretty busy today, isn’t it?
items.followUpQuestion: What brought you here today?
items.retryFocus: Make the opener less generic by using a real detail.
items.braveExtension: Sustain three turns using the shared environment.

items.title: Keep a conversation going with follow-ups
items.listenerRole: The other person mentions a hobby, project, or recent event.
items.prompt: Ask two connected follow-ups and share one detail.
items.communicativeOutcome: Show interest and help them continue.
items.followUpQuestion: What do you enjoy most about it?
items.retryFocus: Replace one yes/no question with an open question.
items.braveExtension: Move from surface information to motivation or feeling.

items.title: Join a group conversation politely
items.listenerRole: People are discussing a topic you understand and you want to contribute.
items.prompt: Connect to the previous speaker, add an example, and invite a response.
items.communicativeOutcome: Enter at a suitable moment and connect to the current topic.
items.followUpQuestion: Has anyone else experienced something similar?
items.retryFocus: Shorten the opening so the contribution arrives sooner.
items.braveExtension: Join, handle an interruption, and return the floor smoothly.

items.title: Respond with empathy
items.listenerRole: Someone tells you about a difficult day or disappointment.
items.prompt: Acknowledge, reflect the feeling, and ask about support.
items.communicativeOutcome: Acknowledge the feeling without immediately giving unwanted advice.
supportPhrases: I can imagine that was frustrating.
What would be helpful right now?
items.followUpQuestion: What would be most helpful right now?
items.retryFocus: Remove one sentence about yourself and return attention to the speaker.
items.braveExtension: Balance empathy, boundaries, and a practical offer.

items.title: Give a natural compliment and continue
items.listenerRole: You notice something positive about a person’s work, choice, or skill.
items.prompt: Explain what you appreciated and respond to the answer.
items.communicativeOutcome: Give a specific sincere compliment and open a short conversation.
supportPhrases: How did you learn to do that?
items.followUpQuestion: What part are you most happy with?
items.retryFocus: Make the compliment more specific than “That’s nice.”
items.braveExtension: Use the compliment to sustain three natural turns.

items.title: End a conversation warmly
items.listenerRole: You need to leave without making the other person feel dismissed.
items.prompt: Refer to something discussed and suggest future contact.
items.communicativeOutcome: Signal the ending, show appreciation, and mention future contact when relevant.
supportPhrases: It was nice talking with you.
I should let you get back to it.
items.followUpQuestion: What is the best way to stay in touch?
items.retryFocus: Add one specific reference so the close feels personal.
items.braveExtension: Close a networking conversation after agreeing one next action.

items.title: Ask for help clearly
items.listenerRole: You are blocked and need help from a busy colleague.
items.prompt: Explain the goal, attempts, blocker, and help needed.
items.communicativeOutcome: Explain what you tried and make a specific reasonable request.
items.followUpQuestion: What have you already tried?
items.retryFocus: Make the request smaller and more actionable.
items.braveExtension: Negotiate another time or smaller request if they are busy.

items.title: Confirm a requirement before starting
items.listenerRole: A request contains unclear scope or success criteria.
items.prompt: Summarise your understanding and ask about scope and success.
items.communicativeOutcome: Confirm what success means before doing the work.
supportPhrases: Would it be correct to say…?
How will we know this is complete?
items.followUpQuestion: What would count as success?
items.retryFocus: Turn one vague question into a choice or measurable condition.
items.braveExtension: Clarify user, outcome, constraints, priority, and acceptance.

items.title: Summarise a meeting decision
items.listenerRole: The meeting is ending after several decisions and actions.
items.prompt: Summarise decision, owners, and deadlines.
items.communicativeOutcome: Leave everyone with the same understanding of owners and timing.
supportPhrases: Before we finish, can we confirm…
items.followUpQuestion: Did I miss any action item?
items.retryFocus: Separate confirmed decisions from ideas still under discussion.
items.braveExtension: Separate decisions from open questions and invite correction.

items.title: Ask for and give useful feedback
items.listenerRole: A colleague shares a draft, or you want feedback on your own work.
items.prompt: Explain the issue’s effect and suggest an action.
items.communicativeOutcome: Make feedback specific, actionable, and respectful.
supportPhrases: One thing that works well is…
One area we could improve is…
Could you focus your feedback on…?
items.followUpQuestion: Which part should be improved first?
items.retryFocus: Make one vague comment observable or measurable.
items.braveExtension: Balance direct feedback with questions and agree a revision.

items.title: Calm an unhappy customer
items.listenerRole: A customer is upset because a service failed.
items.prompt: Confirm the problem, action, and update expectation.
items.communicativeOutcome: Acknowledge the impact, confirm the issue, and explain the next action.
supportPhrases: Let me make sure I understand…
Here’s what I can do next…
items.followUpQuestion: Which outcome would help most?
items.retryFocus: Replace one defensive explanation with a customer-focused action.
items.braveExtension: Handle rejection of the first solution and offer alternatives.

items.title: Recommend a product or place
items.listenerRole: Someone asks what they should buy, eat, visit, or try.
items.prompt: Give two reasons and one limitation.
items.communicativeOutcome: Match a recommendation to their priorities.
supportPhrases: The only thing to keep in mind is…
items.followUpQuestion: What matters most: price, convenience, or quality?
items.retryFocus: Replace one adjective with a practical benefit.
items.braveExtension: Compare two choices and recommend based on budget or preference.

items.title: Resolve a booking mismatch
items.listenerRole: At check-in, the booking does not match your confirmation.
items.prompt: Request the original arrangement and ask about alternatives.
items.communicativeOutcome: Present evidence and negotiate an acceptable alternative.
supportPhrases: There seems to be a difference.
items.followUpQuestion: Would a different time or room work?
items.retryFocus: Use one contrast sentence: I booked X, but the system shows Y.
items.braveExtension: Negotiate another option and confirm cost or conditions.

items.title: Explain directions or a process
items.listenerRole: Someone asks how to reach a place or complete a simple process.
items.prompt: Give the full process and one warning or check.
items.communicativeOutcome: Give ordered instructions with a landmark, warning, or success check.
items.followUpQuestion: Which step is most likely to confuse?
items.retryFocus: Break one long instruction into two short steps.
items.braveExtension: Explain, answer one clarification, and rephrase a confusing step.

items.title: Give an opinion with a clear reason
items.listenerRole: Someone asks what you think about a familiar topic or decision.
items.prompt: Add an example and acknowledge one condition.
items.communicativeOutcome: State the position early and support it with a relevant reason and example.
items.followUpQuestion: What evidence supports that view?
items.retryFocus: Move the position earlier and make the example more specific.
items.braveExtension: Defend the view against a follow-up while remaining open-minded.

items.title: Compare two options fairly
items.listenerRole: A person or team must choose between two realistic options.
items.prompt: Compare on two criteria and recommend.
items.communicativeOutcome: Compare them using shared criteria and make a traceable recommendation.
supportPhrases: Option A is better for…, while…
It depends on what matters most.
items.followUpQuestion: Which criterion matters most?
items.retryFocus: Organise by criteria, not all of A then all of B.
items.braveExtension: Compare cost, risk, and long-term value, then adapt to a changed priority.

items.title: Recommend a solution to a problem
items.listenerRole: A problem has several possible responses and the group asks for your recommendation.
items.prompt: Recommend, explain fit, and propose a first step.
items.communicativeOutcome: Connect the action to the cause, constraints, and desired result.
items.followUpQuestion: What is the smallest safe test?
items.retryFocus: Link every action to a specific cause or result.
items.braveExtension: Choose among alternatives, address risk, and define a small test.

items.title: Challenge a risky idea constructively
items.listenerRole: A group likes an idea, but an important risk has not been discussed.
items.prompt: Explain the consequence and suggest a safer test.
items.communicativeOutcome: Surface the risk without attacking the person or blocking progress.
supportPhrases: I like the goal behind this.
items.followUpQuestion: What evidence would make you comfortable?
items.retryFocus: Replace a vague fear with a cause-and-effect scenario.
items.braveExtension: Challenge it under group pressure and respond to pushback.

items.title: Answer an unexpected question
items.listenerRole: You receive a question you did not prepare for.
items.prompt: Give a structured answer and example.
items.communicativeOutcome: Create a usable answer with a clear position.
items.followUpQuestion: What experience led to that view?
items.retryFocus: Shorten the opening so the direct answer arrives sooner.
items.braveExtension: Answer, qualify your view, and handle a follow-up.

items.title: Explain around a forgotten word
items.listenerRole: You forget an important word while speaking.
items.prompt: Explain around two missing words and finish the story.
items.communicativeOutcome: Describe its category, function, appearance, or example and continue.
supportPhrases: The word is escaping me, but…
items.followUpQuestion: Is it something you use, do, feel, or see?
items.retryFocus: Start with a simple category word, then add the distinguishing detail.
items.braveExtension: Describe a technical or abstract word through definition, example, and contrast.

items.title: Correct yourself without losing flow
items.listenerRole: You notice that an important word, number, or statement was wrong.
items.prompt: Reformulate a confusing sentence more simply.
items.communicativeOutcome: Correct it briefly and continue the main message.
supportPhrases: Let me say that again more clearly.
items.followUpQuestion: Does the correction change the next action?
items.retryFocus: Reduce the repair to one signal and one corrected sentence.
items.braveExtension: Correct a factual mistake and explain whether the conclusion changes.

items.title: Speak with no preparation
items.listenerRole: A familiar topic appears and recording begins immediately.
items.prompt: Speak for one minute and use one saved phrase.
items.communicativeOutcome: Use mostly familiar English to complete the message under light pressure.
supportPhrases: The first thing that comes to mind is…
items.followUpQuestion: What is one example?
items.retryFocus: Repeat with a clearer opening, not harder vocabulary.
items.braveExtension: Speak for 90 seconds, handle a follow-up, and summarise.

items.title: Big 30 question remix
items.listenerRole: Answer several familiar personal questions in a random order.
items.prompt: Answer three questions and one follow-up.
items.communicativeOutcome: Retrieve personal content flexibly rather than reciting one fixed script.
items.followUpQuestion: Which answer needs a stronger example?
items.retryFocus: Change one opening so the answers do not sound identical.
items.braveExtension: Complete a rapid five-question interview.

items.title: Big 30 question remix
items.listenerRole: Answer several familiar personal questions in a random order.
items.prompt: Answer three questions and one follow-up.
items.communicativeOutcome: Retrieve personal content flexibly rather than reciting one fixed script.
items.followUpQuestion: Which answer needs a stronger example?
items.retryFocus: Change one opening so the answers do not sound identical.
items.braveExtension: Complete a rapid five-question interview.

items.title: Personal goal simulation
items.listenerRole: Choose the real situation that originally motivated you to improve English.
items.prompt: Complete it with one follow-up or obstacle.
items.communicativeOutcome: Complete a realistic simulation that matters to your life.
items.followUpQuestion: What would the other person say next?
items.retryFocus: Repeat the part most likely to happen in real life.
items.braveExtension: Run the full scenario with two unexpected turns.

repairLab.label: Repair Lab
repairLab.purpose: Keep communication moving when the learner freezes, forgets a word, misunderstands, gets interrupted, or needs to correct a message.

items.title: Buy time instead of freezing
items.breakdownScenario: You are asked an unexpected question and your mind goes blank.
rescuePhrases: Let me think for a second.
I haven’t thought about that before, but…
items.task: Answer after using one time-buying phrase.
items.modelRepair: That’s a good question. I think the main reason is convenience.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Ask for repetition
items.breakdownScenario: You did not hear the last part of a question.
rescuePhrases: Sorry, could you say that again?
Could you repeat the last part?
Could you say that a little more slowly?
items.task: Ask for exactly what you need instead of saying only “What?”
items.modelRepair: Sorry, could you repeat the part about the deadline?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Clarify vague instructions
rescuePhrases: When you say ___, do you mean…?
items.task: Clarify the deadline and expected result.
items.modelRepair: Just to clarify, would you like the revised report by the end of today?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Soften disagreement
items.breakdownScenario: A colleague suggests releasing a change without testing.
items.task: Acknowledge the idea, state the risk, and offer an alternative.
items.modelRepair: I see your point, but one concern is the risk of new errors. Could we run a short test first?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Repair an unclear explanation
items.breakdownScenario: The listener says, “I’m not sure I follow.”
rescuePhrases: Let me explain that another way.
items.task: Restate the message using simpler words and one example.
items.modelRepair: What I mean is that the system is working, but one permission is missing. For example, normal users cannot open the page.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Enter or return after interruption
items.breakdownScenario: Two people are talking and you have a relevant point, or someone interrupts you.
items.task: Enter politely or return to your unfinished point.
items.modelRepair: Can I add something here? We saw the same issue last month, and the cause was a missing setting.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Respond with empathy
items.breakdownScenario: Someone tells you they had a very stressful week.
rescuePhrases: I can imagine that was stressful.
I’m sorry you had to deal with that.
items.task: Acknowledge the feeling before giving advice or changing the topic.
items.modelRepair: That sounds really difficult. Did you manage to get any rest over the weekend?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Take responsibility for a delay
items.breakdownScenario: A task will not be finished at the promised time.
rescuePhrases: I wanted to let you know early…
items.task: Explain the cause briefly, give a new time, and state your action.
items.modelRepair: I wanted to let you know early that we’re running behind because one file arrived late. I expect to finish tomorrow morning.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Confirm a requirement
items.breakdownScenario: A request contains several possible interpretations.
items.task: Summarise your understanding and ask one targeted question.
items.modelRepair: From my understanding, you need a weekly Excel report for managers. Have I understood correctly?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Handle vague feedback
items.breakdownScenario: Someone says, “This is not quite right.”
rescuePhrases: Could you show me which part…?
What would a better result look like?
items.task: Ask for one concrete example and the priority.
items.modelRepair: Could you show me which section is not working for you, and what the most important change would be?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: De-escalate an unhappy customer
items.breakdownScenario: A customer says, “This is unacceptable. I’ve waited all day.”
rescuePhrases: Here’s what I can do now…
items.task: Acknowledge, apologise appropriately, and offer a concrete next step.
items.modelRepair: I understand why you’re frustrated, and I’m sorry about the delay. I’ll check the status now and update you within fifteen minutes.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Resolve a booking mismatch
items.breakdownScenario: The hotel cannot find the room type shown in your confirmation.
items.task: State the evidence, ask for a check, and propose an acceptable alternative.
items.modelRepair: According to my confirmation, I booked a double room for tonight. Could you check the booking number again?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Explain a trade-off when challenged
items.breakdownScenario: Someone asks, “Why not just choose the cheapest option?”
rescuePhrases: It may cost less now, although…
items.task: Explain the hidden cost without dismissing the question.
items.modelRepair: It costs less now, but the trade-off is higher maintenance. Over a year, the second option may be more economical.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Challenge a risky idea
items.breakdownScenario: A senior colleague proposes an option you believe is unsafe.
rescuePhrases: Could we reduce the risk by…?
items.task: Use a question or evidence, not a personal attack.
items.modelRepair: May I raise one concern? What happens if the change fails in production? Could we reduce the risk with a pilot?
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Speak around a forgotten word
items.breakdownScenario: You forget the exact English word in the middle of an answer.
rescuePhrases: I don’t know the exact word, but…
items.task: Describe function, appearance, location, or an example and continue.
items.modelRepair: I don’t know the exact word, but it’s the small device you use to connect the cable to the laptop.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Recover your turn
items.breakdownScenario: Someone interrupts before you complete your point.
rescuePhrases: I’ll come to that in a moment.
items.task: Protect your turn politely, then finish in one sentence.
items.modelRepair: I’ll come to that in a moment. Just to complete the thought, we need approval before we can deploy.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Correct yourself without restarting
items.breakdownScenario: You give the wrong date, name, number, or tense.
items.task: Correct only the necessary detail and continue.
items.modelRepair: The meeting is on Thursday - sorry, let me correct that - Friday at two, and I’ll send the agenda tomorrow.
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

items.title: Make a next-step plan after feedback
items.breakdownScenario: After a simulation, you realise one part was unclear.
rescuePhrases: The part I want to improve is…
A clearer way to say it is…
items.task: Name one specific improvement and immediately try the revised line.
items.modelRepair: The part I want to improve is my ending. A clearer way to say it is: ‘My recommendation is to test it with one team next week.’
items.reflection: Did the repair keep the conversation moving?

fluencySprint.label: Fluency Sprint
fluencySprint.purpose: Repeat a familiar message under gradually changing time and support conditions.

items.title: Introduction sprint
items.focus: Keep the same message but reduce long pauses.
items.followUpQuestion: What could the listener ask next?

items.title: Story sprint
items.focus: Make the sequence easier to follow.
items.followUpQuestion: What did you learn or feel?
items.rule: Finish the story in every round.

items.title: Memory sprint
items.topic: Describe a memorable trip or event.
items.focus: Use one vivid detail and one clear ending.
items.followUpQuestion: Would you like to experience it again?

items.title: Retell for smoothness
items.topic: Retell a story you practised earlier.
items.focus: Round 2: fewer pauses. Round 3: clearer emphasis.
items.followUpQuestion: Which version felt most natural?
items.rule: Keep content mostly constant across rounds.

items.title: Social conversation sprint
items.topic: Start, continue, and close a short conversation.
items.focus: Make each move sound connected rather than memorised.
items.followUpQuestion: What follow-up could keep it going?
items.rule: Use at least one real question.

items.title: Workplace checkpoint
items.topic: Give an update and respond to a follow-up.
items.followUpQuestion: What support do you need?

items.title: Voice-message sprint
items.focus: Make names, numbers, and actions easy to catch.
items.followUpQuestion: When should they respond?
items.rule: No visual notes in the final round.

items.title: Service recovery sprint
items.topic: Handle a customer or booking problem.
items.focus: Stay calm and make the request specific.
items.followUpQuestion: What compromise would you accept?

items.title: Mini-presentation rehearsal
items.focus: Use clear signposts and a strong ending.
items.followUpQuestion: What objection might the audience raise?
items.rule: Do not read a full script.

items.title: Unexpected-question sprint
items.topic: Answer a question you did not prepare.
items.focus: Start with a clear answer before explaining.
items.followUpQuestion: What could change your answer?
items.rule: One brief thinking phrase is allowed.

items.title: No-preparation rotation
items.focus: Switch topics without trying to be perfect.
items.followUpQuestion: Which topic was hardest and why?

items.title: Three-round fluency test
items.focus: Round 1 complete; Round 2 smoother; Round 3 more natural.
items.followUpQuestion: Which pause could you remove?

items.title: Big 30 remix
items.topic: Answer two common personal questions back-to-back.
items.focus: Avoid sounding like two separate scripts.
items.followUpQuestion: What common theme connects the answers?

items.title: Personal-goal simulation
items.topic: Practise the situation that matters most to you.
items.focus: Make the outcome practical and personal.
items.followUpQuestion: What would success look like?

items.title: Day 1 comparison
items.topic: Answer the Day 1 introduction prompt again.
items.focus: Notice progress rather than chasing perfection.
items.followUpQuestion: What can you do now that was harder on Day 1?

items.title: Final speaking showcase
items.topic: Combine a story, opinion, and future plan.
items.focus: Show flexible communication and use repair if needed.
items.followUpQuestion: What will your next 30 days focus on?
